steps.decide: What the person must be able to do after this flow, and the smallest sequence that proves it
Which steps are required versus optional, and how skipping is offered without shame
How progress, save-and-resume and interruption are handled
What happens when a step fails, and how the partial state is preserved
How the flow ends: what is created, what is shown next, and how to change it later

rules.statement: The flow exists to get one real thing done, so step one does work, not setup: the first screen asks only what the product cannot infer.
Anything that can be changed later is skippable, and skipping is a plain link, never a red 'No thanks' or a guilt trip.
Progress is stored server-side per step; returning to the flow offers to resume where it stopped, and abandoning it leaves the account usable.
A failed step keeps everything already entered, names the failing field and stays on the step; it never restarts the flow.
The last screen lands in the real workspace with the created thing visible, and says how to change it; a confetti screen that returns to nothing is not an ending.
Progress states the step count and the current step in text, and each step change announces it politely; the indicator is never colour-only.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a step submission applies only to the step revision it was sent for; a late response from an abandoned step never advances the flow

sections.intent: Get a new person to one completed, real task in the product, and leave them with an account they can use even if they stop halfway.
useCases: create the first workspace and invite one colleague
connect one data source and see real numbers
nicheDifferences: Onboarding is the only flow a person meets before they trust the product, so its job is to be short and honest: every extra field is evidence that the product will be tedious later.
inputs: the one outcome the flow must produce
what the product can infer instead of asking
where progress is stored and for how long
anatomy: a step count and title in text
one question per step with a visible label
a primary action and a quieter skip link
an inline error region per step
a final screen showing the created thing
styling: one column, one primary action per screen, no competing navigation
the progress indicator is text plus a thin bar, never colour-only
the skip link is visually quiet but keyboard-reachable
a11y: each step change moves focus to the step heading and announces the new step
the progress indicator has a text equivalent and is not an ARIA progressbar that lies about time
errors are associated with their field and announced
the flow is fully operable with keyboard and screen reader, including skip
responsive: the flow is one column at every width; below 480 px the primary action becomes full-width and sticky above the safe area
keyboard-triggered fields use the right keyboard types on mobile
long translated step titles wrap instead of truncating
copy: each step asks one question in the person's words, with an example
the skip link names what happens: 'Skip for now — you can connect this later in Settings'
the final screen says what exists now and what to do next
alternatives: inline setup inside the workspace for people who prefer to explore
a guided checklist that lives on the dashboard instead of blocking first use
import from an existing workspace when migrating a team

references.label: WAI-ARIA APG — focus management in multi-step flows

acceptance: the first screen asks only what cannot be inferred
every optional step is skippable through a plain link that says what happens
closing the flow halfway leaves a usable account and offers resume on return
a failed step preserves entered values and stays on the step
the final screen lands in the workspace with the created thing visible
failureCases: the flow restarts after a failure and the person re-enters everything
skipping is hidden, so people abandon the product at step two
the final screen is a celebration with no product behind it
progress is stored only in the tab, so a refresh loses the flow
